D7.name: Right top plate (one piece with P6)
D7.note: Adam: “new additional bridge plate for easier access and assembly.. this one will boolean with the plate above it.” (typed 2026-11-13; it landed on the Work surface, moved here). Claude: cut it flat from 1/4" faced to 3.3 and solvent-weld it under P6 (dowels line the two up), so both stay one-sided cuts on the Z1; in the sim it stays its own drawn part. Screws C4–C6 pass through it.

D5.name: P5 crescent
D5.note: Claude: a bridge between the minute wheel and the right top plate, around the transfer pinion. A steady pin in P4 locates it, so it sits still while the top plate goes on; screw C7 (from P6’s top, through it and P4 into P3) then clamps it. 0.3 mm gap to the right top plate. Needs Adam: what it should carry, if anything.

D8.name: Left bridge
D8.note: Claude: fills the left of the motion layer around the minute wheel (tips + 0.75). The hour rod passes through a slot at its edge: the minute wheel is too close for a bearing here, so the hour rod runs in bearings in P2 and P4 instead. Clamped by screws C1–C3, located by dowel 1. 0.3 mm gap to the right top plate.

D6.name: P6 top plate
D6.note: Claude: recessed for both discs (0.5 under each, 0.7 round the rim) with openings the disc units drop through. The minute wheel arbor’s top pivot is a plain 3.05 hole between the recesses (no room for a bearing; it turns once in 4 hours).

hour.note: Hour wheel and hour disc are one piece, bonded through a Ø30 × 0.5 hub so the disc clears the minute pinion by 0.5: the unit drops in from the top and presses onto the hour rod like a hand. The rod runs in bearings in P2 and P4 (12.5 mm apart), with a collar above P4’s bearing for end shake.

center.note: Transfer pinion (12 teeth, 2.8 thick, meshing with the minute wheel) and the minute disc are one piece, joined by a hub up through P6 (29.1–33.0, under Ø14.6 so it passes the opening; the sim has no hub part, so it shows a gap): it drops in from the top, through P6 and the crescent, onto the transfer tube that grips the Slava center arbor. Turning the disc sets the time.

project.name: Hemistitch + Slava donor
project.title: Hemistitch · Slava 5671 engine
project.blurb: Phase 1 of the fully mechanical plan: a Slava 5671 alarm-clock movement (Swiss lever, 18,000 beats an hour) is the engine. Its barrel, train, escapement and balance stay in its own plates; we tap its center arbor for our motion works and the two discs. Slava parts are bought, and their sizes are estimates from the 1987 factory manual until the clock arrives. Our parts are module 1 in 2.8 mm acrylic.
source: Slava 5671: Shamonova, Repair of Mechanical Alarm Clocks (1987): 55.8 mm, 19 mm deep, 11 jewels, free (Swiss) lever, 15-tooth escape wheel, brass balance with a 0.4 s period, both springs in barrels, 36 h per wind, friction cannon pinion on the center arbor. Arbor positions are scaled from its Fig. 1 drawing; tooth counts and the balance diameter are guesses, to measure on the real one. Discs and motion works: VISION §10.8.

focus.label: Slava engine: barrel → center → third → seconds → escape → balance
Motion works and discs: center → minute wheel → hour wheel

rules.why: the 1 mm end mill has to fit between the pinion teeth

arbors.name: Slava going barrel
arbors.role: Bought (Slava). The mainspring (2.9 × 0.2 × 611 mm) in a closed barrel, inside about Ø20.8; at least 36 hours per wind. Drives the center pinion. Position, tooth count and size are estimates (about 13.5 mm from the center arbor, so its teeth stay inside the movement’s Ø55.8); measure the real one.

arbors.name: Center arbor
arbors.role: The Slava’s center arbor: turns once an hour. Inside the Slava its pinion is driven by the barrel and its wheel drives the third wheel. Above the Slava our transfer tube (3 mm OD brass, in bearings in P4 and P6) slips over it and grips it by friction, so you can still set the time. The tube carries our module-1 transfer gear in P5, which drives the minute wheel, and the minute disc on top.

arbors.name: Third wheel (Slava)
arbors.role: Bought (Slava): the intermediate wheel. Position scaled from the manual’s drawing; tooth counts are guesses.

arbors.name: Seconds wheel (Slava)
arbors.role: Bought (Slava): turns once a minute and drives the escape pinion. Tooth counts are guesses.

arbors.name: Escape wheel (Slava)
arbors.role: Bought (Slava): 15 club teeth (confirmed), jeweled pivots. At 18,000 beats an hour it turns every 6 seconds, released half a tooth per beat. Size estimated.

arbors.name: Pallet fork (Slava)
arbors.role: Bought (Slava): the jeweled pallet fork, shown as the space it sweeps. Between the escape wheel and the balance, in line with both (Playtner’s proportions). It rocks each beat; the sim doesn’t animate that yet.

arbors.name: Balance (Slava)
arbors.role: Bought (Slava): brass balance with its hairspring, a 0.4 s swing (18,000 beats an hour), under its own cock on the back: the beating heart behind the case-back window. About Ø15 and about 18 mm from the center arbor, both estimated from the manual’s drawing. It swings; the sim doesn’t animate that yet.

arbors.name: Minute wheel
arbors.role: Ours. Its 3 mm rod turns in bearings in P4 and P6. The transfer gear turns its 48-tooth wheel 4:1 (in P5); its 14-leaf pinion turns the hour wheel 3:1 (in the pocket under P6), so 12:1 in all.

arbors.name: Hour wheel
arbors.role: Ours. Its 3 mm rod turns in bearings in P4 and P6; the wheel sits in the pocket under P6, turns once in 12 hours, and the hour disc is pressed on the rod above the top plate.

hands.name: Minute disc
hands.role: Ours: 2.8 mm acrylic, Ø47.5, on the transfer tube 0.5 mm above the top plate. One turn an hour; the minutes pass the index at 3 o’clock.

hands.name: Hour disc
hands.role: Ours: 2.8 mm acrylic, Ø47.5, fixed on top of the hour wheel. One number passes the index at 3 o’clock each hour.

plate.name: Work surface
plate.role: Just the ground under the model; the movement’s real plates are the six drawn parts P1–P6. Yellow outlines: the AXIS case grown 2.5× with its top and bottom bow deepened to 4.25 mm (reference), and the Slava movement’s Ø55.8 footprint at its back and its front (estimated position: rotated so its balance points at the case’s center line).
